source_metadata.title: Characterization of a Catalase-Negative Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Strain
source_metadata.source_type: clinical isolate characterization / case report note
source_metadata.batching: not required; 2-page source processed as one semantic unit

atoms.canonical_statement: The report aimed to molecularly characterize a catalase-negative methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus subsp. aureus clinical isolate by amplification and sequencing of its catalase gene.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We here describe a catalase-negative methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) isolate that was characterized by amplification and sequencing of the putative catalase gene.

atoms.canonical_statement: The isolate was recovered from a tracheal secretion specimen from a 65-year-old multimorbid male admitted to a surgical intensive care unit; no signs of infection were apparent when the specimen was collected.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A 65-year-old male was admitted to the intensive care unit... A tracheal secretion sample was taken for routine microbiological investigation, without signs of any infection being apparent at that time.

atoms.canonical_statement: The isolate repeatedly tested catalase-negative after aerobic and anaerobic incubation through the fifth subculture while growing well under both aerobic and anaerobic conditions.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The isolate repeatedly tested negative for catalase after either aerobic or anaerobic incubation, even at the fifth subculture. It grew well both aerobically and anaerobically.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors distinguished the isolate from S. aureus subsp. anaerobius and S. saccharolyticus by its aerobic growth, clumping-factor expression, acid production from trehalose and lactose, and 16S rRNA sequence.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Our strain differs from these species on the basis of its ability to grow well under aerobic conditions, its expression of clumping factor, its production of acid from trehalose and lactose, and its 16S rRNA sequence.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that the available reports indicate catalase is not an absolute requirement for S. aureus pathogenicity, while acknowledging that pathogenicity or transmission efficiency could be decreased.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Although few, these reports do provide evidence that catalase is not an absolute requirement for pathogenicity. However, it is possible that pathogenicity or transmission efficiency is decreased.

atoms.canonical_statement: In this case, the catalase-negative MRSA was repeatedly isolated only from the same patient, was not recovered from other hospital patients, and was not linked to apparent infection, limiting inference about pathogenicity and transmissibility.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the catalase-negative MRSA strain was repeatedly isolated from the same patient but never from other patients ... There were no indications that the strain had caused an infection.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors presented the strain as the first catalase-negative S. aureus subsp. aureus strain characterized with molecular methods.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This is also the first report of a catalase-negative S. aureus subsp. aureus strain characterized with molecular methods.

atoms.canonical_statement: The catalase-gene sequence from the isolate was deposited in GenBank under accession EF140590.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The catalase gene sequence identified in this study was submitted to GenBank under accession no. EF140590.
